answer.rationale: finance_justification: memory_c4 shows benchmarking at renewal moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms; memory_c6 shows multi-year commitment unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope. Combining those two levers—renewing the incumbent on a longer term while benchmarking against market rates—addresses the 18% cost cut while keeping the existing supply relationship intact. memory_c2 is noted but a primary-vendor switch is rejected: onboarding lead-time conflicts with the 14-day expiry and the assembly line running at 94% with no buffer; a switch at this cadence adds delivery risk that violates the constraint. A second source (memory_c3) would add cost rather than cut it, so it is deferred. Deferral (memory_c5) is not viable because the contract does not auto-renew and lapse would stop deliveries. Scope is deliberately narrow: one negotiation with the incumbent, benchmarked, term-extended, with no vendor change and no scope change.
